about: Regression cases for kai review-commit: real defects from kaicontext/kai-cli's own history, each flagged by a reviewer on one push and corrected by a later fix commit, so the defect is confirmed. None comes from Martian's Code Review Bench: cases taken from the benchmark (the six this corpus held until 2026-09-30) teach the reviewer the test it is scored on. base/head are the PR's base and the buggy head; heads that never reached main are fetched by SHA (refs/pull/N/head). 'expect' is a defect Kai must publish: a published claim matches when it names the file and contains one of 'any' (case-insensitive). 'forbid' is a finding Kai must not publish; 'at_most' caps how many published claims may match, for one root cause posted several times. Run with scripts/review-regressions.sh.

expect.golden: A repeated FINDINGS:/ISSUES: header in rcParseReviewOutput only switches `section` back to issues; the earlier (quoted example) block's risks, INTENT_MATCH verdict, matchConflict flag and note are not reset, so quoted bullets are published as findings and a quoted `INTENT_MATCH: diverges` above the real `verified` flips the verdict to unknown, contrary to the commit's claim that a second header supersedes the whole block.

rcGrepIdentifiers runs `git grep` via exec.Command(...).Output() with no context, timeout, WaitDelay or output cap, before the review's first model turn, so a grep for common identifiers in a large repository can run for tens of minutes (or hang) and consume the whole review's time budget.

The workflow_dispatch ref inputs are spliced into the run script as REF='${{ inputs.kai_cli_ref }}' (and the tui/engine/core refs); GitHub substitutes the expression into the script text before bash parses it, so a ref containing a single quote closes the string and runs arbitrary shell in the job that then authenticates to GCP and pushes the production image; the inputs should be passed through env.

The coverage gate resumes the first run's session, and a resumed run's Transcript is the whole conversation (first pass included), so `inc.Turns += rcTurns(res2.Transcript)` counts the first pass's turns twice and the manifest over-reports turns; it should assign, not add.

shipIsMergeSubject treats any subject that starts with "merge " and contains " into " as a merge commit, so an ordinary change such as "merge the two handlers into one function" is skipped by shipFirstCommitSubject and the branch loses its descriptive name, the very regression the commit set out to fix; only git's merge wordings and the refresh's two-bare-ref "merge <ref> into <ref>" form should match.

runShipPromote's failure rollback calls gitio.DiscardChanges (reset --hard) and then os.Remove on every non-delete file the apply loop wrote, including files that already existed at HEAD and were just restored by the reset, so a failed promote deletes tracked files from the source repo's working tree; only files the apply created should be removed.

Pin runs now also read the dashboard issue body, append their entry and write it back with `gh issue edit`, but pin and nightly runs sit in different concurrency groups (review-regressions-<pin_pr> vs review-regressions-nightly), so two runs finishing together each read the same body and the second write silently drops the first run's history entry.

The gate's grep reports a failed or timed-out search only when git produced no output (both checks are gated on len(out) == 0), so a search killed by its 15s timeout or stopped at the 1 MiB read cap after emitting partial stdout is returned as a complete match list, letting the gate cite a missing match as proof of absence.
